title: Grandma's Lake Glows After NOON 🌙
premise: At Grandma's lake, swimming is free all morning and banned after noon, because the moon sleeps on the lake bed all day and swimmers wake it, and a moon that wakes goes up. I help Grandma at the lake every weekend. One hot afternoon I swim anyway, and the sky starts going dark. That night I follow her rowboat out, and watch her push the moon up with her oar.
twist: Grandma has pushed the moon up into the sky with her oar every night for fifty years, and the rule is there because swimmers wake it. When her arms are too tired one night, I swim down and wake it on purpose, and now we lift it together.
world: A bright summer lake ringed with pines: a gray wooden dock, a red rowboat, a white lake house with a green screen porch, and a pale glow under the water where the moon sleeps.
